...unlimited contributions? Like, directly to the party/candidate? There are laws to prevent these. The Federal Elections Campaign Act limited individual contributions to candidates to $1,000 (although this was doubled by the Bipartisan Campaign Reform Act). This same act also limited soft money contributions to state parties to $10,000 and limits that money to simply promoting the party, not particular candidate. Ontop of this it completely banned soft money donations to national parties. FECA made it so all candidates must reveal who contributed to their campaign and how much, and it began a form of public fundraising. PACs, while many rally against them, are also limited by this act to $5,000 per candidate per election. While Super PACs are not limited at all, nor also really 527 groups, neither of these groups are directly involved with the candidates or parties. They simply have a preference and spend money to promote what they believe in. While our political system and financing is by no means perfect, these blanket statement about how it is completely broken and no effort is being made is a logical fallacy.
